$description: Pokeapp design tokens — consolidated v1. Platform-agnostic, W3C DTCG-flavored. Light/dark given as sibling values on each token rather than separate files, for simplicity at this scale. Extracted from and validated against: hero detail POC, Pokedex grid POC, species detail (two-panel) POC, team-build form POC.

900.$description: Primary ink, light mode text / dark mode surface

800.$description: Dark-gray, used specifically for button-primary-fill in light mode — deliberately not full ink.900 black, reads a shade softer

900.$description: Primary text on dark surfaces / light-mode near-white

light.$description: Drawer / floating-panel surface, light — lighter than base surface

dark.$description: Drawer / floating-panel surface, dark — lighter than base surface

light.$description: Pointer-hover tone, light — a step DOWN from surface-raised, which is the top of the light ramp. Carries ~3x the luminance delta of surface against surface-raised (0.129 vs 0.044); the 2% surface step was too faint on white. Still short of the hairline, so a hovered row does not read as a filled band.

dark.$description: Pointer-hover tone, dark — same value as surface.dark, which already read correctly against surface-raised.dark. A token of its own so light can diverge without dragging dark with it.

light.$description: Signature accent, grounded in real Pokedex device red, not a generic palette pick

dark.$description: Brightened for contrast against dark surface

stat-increase.$description: The up-arrow beside a nature's raised stat. Deliberately NOT accent-red: --accent has exactly four sanctioned uses (active tab/nav, binary indicator, error/validation, stat magnitude on a base-stat bar) and 'this stat went up' is none of them — a nature's direction arrow is not a magnitude. Contrast computed the same way the type palettes were, and the light/dark pair is matched to its stat-decrease counterpart so neither arrow reads as louder than the other. RGB distance from accent-red is 42 (light) and 70 (dark), far enough not to be mistaken for it.

stat-decrease.$description: The down-arrow beside a nature's lowered stat. Blue against stat-increase's red, matched for contrast rather than for hue symmetry.

type-color.$description: RETIRED, kept for the record — no longer used anywhere in the app. The dev-time choice between this muted palette and type-color-community is closed: the community palette won and is now the only type palette, app-wide, in both themes and on every screen. Nothing references these values; see type-color-community and its two per-mode override sets. All 17 types in Gen 1-4 scope (Fairy excluded — Gen 6).

type-color-community.$description: THE type palette, app-wide, in both themes — the muted type-color group above is retired. The de facto community-standard type hex set (originally from the games' own type-chart UI, widely paired with PokeAPI though not returned by it). These raw values are the reference hue; neither mode uses all 17 of them unmodified, because the set was drawn for type-chart FILLS with text on top, not for coloured text. Dark mode: 12 of 17 clear a >=4:1 floor against #141414 as published, the other 5 are in type-color-community-dark-mode-override. Light mode: only 5 of 17 clear the floor against #fafafa and the other 12 are in type-color-community-light-mode-override — the two sets are exact complements, which is what you would expect of mid-dark saturated colours versus bright pastels.

type-color-community-dark-mode-override.$description: Only these 5 needed a computed dark-mode lift; the other 12 in type-color-community already clear the >=4:1 floor unmodified.

type-color-community-light-mode-override.$description: The other twelve. Computed exactly as the dark-mode set was, mirrored: each community hue mixed toward BLACK until it reaches >=4:1 against the light surface #fafafa, rather than toward white against #141414. Scaling all three channels equally preserves hue and saturation, so each stays recognisably its community colour — Electric is still that yellow — only dark enough to read as text. Measured unmodified contrast, worst first: electric 1.43, ice 1.53, ground 1.69, steel 1.86, grass 1.98, bug 2.11, normal 2.36, rock 2.48, flying 2.54, fire 2.57, water 2.94, psychic 2.98. Fighting, Poison, Ghost, Dragon and Dark are absent here because they already clear the floor in light mode — and they are exactly the five that needed the dark-mode lift.

type-color-dark-mode-override.$description: Dark-mode variant for every type in type-color, now resolved (previously only 'dark' was tested). Computed via actual WCAG relative-luminance contrast against #141414, each lightened (mixed toward white) until reaching >=4:1 — a deliberate floor between 'no check at all' and full WCAG AA, consistent with the project's 'good contrast, not full compliance' bar. 'dark' keeps its earlier hand-picked value (#a89484, tested against real Umbreon artwork) rather than the computed one, since it already exceeds the floor. The other 16 are computed, not hand-art-directed — treat as verified-sufficient, not necessarily the most beautiful possible choice; further eyeballing is optional polish, not a blocker.

flying.$description: Already met the contrast floor unlightened.

bug.$description: Already met the contrast floor unlightened.

ghost.$description: Was the worst offender at 1.9:1 in light-mode-value-on-dark-bg — needed the largest correction.

dark.$description: Hand-picked earlier, tested against real Umbreon artwork — kept as-is, exceeds the computed floor.

surface-raised.$description: Elevation without shadow: a lighter/darker tone-step instead of a drop shadow. Used for the detail-page drawer. This is the system's only elevation mechanism.

surface-hover.$description: Pointer-feedback fill for a row inside a floating panel. Exists because accent-red has exactly four sanctioned uses and hover is not one of them, so hover needs a tone rather than borrowing hairline (a border token) or surface (whose light step is imperceptible against surface-raised).

stat-increase.$description: Up-arrow colour beside a nature's raised stat. A fourth semantic colour alongside accent — added rather than reusing accent, whose four sanctioned uses do not include stat direction.

stat-decrease.$description: Down-arrow colour beside a nature's lowered stat.

surface-species-tint.$description: Data-driven, not a fixed value. Populated per species from a species_id -> {bg_light, bg_dark} lookup table (implementation task, not a design token). Falls back to semantic.surface when no per-species data exists yet. Applies to the detail page's artwork panel only — surface-raised (the drawer) never changes.

accent.$description: Reserved for exactly four functional uses: active tab/nav state, binary state indicators (e.g. caught toggle), error/validation emphasis (confirmed in the form-field-states work, see DESIGN-SYSTEM.md section 8), and stat magnitude — the filled portion of a base-stat bar on the species detail page. The fourth reverses an earlier decision on purpose: base stats were once specified as a plain data table, and the real Figma prototype for the species page uses accent-filled horizontal bars. Never decoration, never more than one element type per screen. CONFIRMED app-wide, not namespaced: this red now also affects the old (pre-redesign) modules that share the --accent variable, replacing their previous purple. Deliberate — those modules are getting replaced eventually, and the color clash is a reasonable 'not yet migrated' signal rather than a bug worth engineering around.

button-primary-fill.$description: Inverts between modes rather than using the accent. Primary actions stay monochrome. Light mode deliberately uses ink.800 (dark gray), not full ink.900 black — a softer primary action fill.

ghost-watermark.$description: The oversized background dex-number treatment. Always rendered at opacity.ghost-watermark regardless of mode or scale.

Constant across hero (220px) and grid (64px) scale, but NOT across modes: 5% white on a near-black surface reads far stronger than 5% black on a near-white one, so a single value cannot match the reference in both. Same kind of light/dark asymmetry as the type-color dark-mode overrides — not a special case.

body.$description: Locked as of the font-alternatives review. Self-hosted webfont, not a system stack — requires bundling the actual .woff2 files (offline-first PWA, no CDN dependency). Fallbacks are the previous system-humanist pick, used only if the bundled font fails to load. IMPLEMENTATION CONFIRMED: variable font file (one .woff2 per subset, ~75 KiB total, wght 100-700), not static per-weight instances from @fontsource. Verified during implementation that weight 600 is a genuine design master within the variable file, not an interpolation — so nothing is lost by choosing the variable file over static instances, and it's simpler to maintain.

numeric.$description: Dex numbers and stat/EV values only. Never names, labels, or body copy — and never the ghost watermark, which is display type and takes font-family.body (see DESIGN-SYSTEM.md section 2). Martian Mono leads, with JetBrains Mono behind it as a second self-hosted fallback. Both are self-hosted (variable, wght 100-800, latin + latin-ext), so nothing here can fall through to an unbundled system font — the stack previously started with 'SF Mono', which left the numeric face resolving to a system font on any machine that has it.

display.$description: Hero species name on the detail page. The one deliberately loud text element.

title.$description: Secondary headings, e.g. species name in a form context.

label.$description: Uppercase field labels, section labels, secondary metadata.

font-weight.$description: Two weights in practice: 400 for body/inputs, 600-700 for names/labels/emphasis. No in-between weights used.

drawer.$description: The detail-page info drawer. Deliberately more pronounced than radius.card.

badge-square.$description: The sanctioned solid-square type badge — deliberately smaller radius than radius.pill, closer to a device-button than a SaaS chip.

radius.$description: Soft/rounded throughout. No sharp corners anywhere in the validated POCs.

gap-xl.$description: Wide gutters, e.g. the two-column form layout.

elevation.$description: No drop shadows anywhere, in either mode — validated across every POC including forms. The system's actual elevation mechanism is a tone-step (semantic.surface vs semantic.surface-raised), not a shadow. If a future component seems to need a shadow, treat that as a signal to reconsider the layout or reach for surface-raised, not a gap to fill with box-shadow.

icon.$description: Base library: Tabler Icons (MIT, 5,900+, matches the previous pokeapp system's choice — reconsidered deliberately, not defaulted into). Grid and stroke locked after a direct visual comparison against tighter/looser alternatives.

variant.$description: Outline matches the system's no-fill, hairline-driven language by default. Filled/duotone is reserved for active or emphasized states rather than relying on color change alone.

active-state-rule.$value: Swap to Tabler's filled variant of the same icon on active/emphasized state, instead of or in addition to a color change.
active-state-rule.$description: Fallback required: Tabler only ships a filled twin for a subset of icons, not all of them (unlike Material Symbols' continuous fill axis, which covers everything by construction — evaluated and not adopted, see design system notes). Where no filled variant exists for a given icon, fall back to a color/weight change instead. This means the active-state treatment will not be perfectly uniform across every icon — a known, accepted gap, not an oversight.

color.$description: Per-context — icons are not locked to ink/paper-only or accent-only. Decide per use the same way any other element's color is decided.

custom-icons-needed.$description: Domain-specific icons Tabler won't have, need hand-design in the same 24px/1.5px convention. Confirmed: type glyphs (17), caught/not-caught (Poke Ball motif), evolution indicator (DNA icon, rotated — continuity from the previous system's convention).

locked.shiny-indicator: Star-burst, filled, yellow — option A from the 12-category review.
locked.nature-stat-boost: Chevron up (red) / chevron down (blue) pair — option B.
locked.region-generation-badge: Flag-shape badge with vertical internal fold lines — option C, modified per feedback (fold lines not yet drawn, follow-up needed).

custom-icons-needed.still-searching: Sprite view toggle, move category (Physical/Special/Status), contest conditions (Cool/Beautiful/Cute/Smart/Tough), item category icons, berry icon, type-effectiveness marker, held-item indicator — user is sourcing these from Tabler/Icones/game-icons.net rather than from the quick-sketch options reviewed.

ledger-dim-rule.$value: Dex number opacity ties to caught/not-caught status, the app's only tracked binary state — not a separate 'seen' concept, since that isn't tracked anywhere else in the app.
ledger-dim-rule.$description: Artwork/sprite itself is unaffected either way — no silhouette-until-caught system. That would be a real feature decision (spoiler-hiding unseen species), out of scope for this token, not an oversight.

focus.$value: Bottom border becomes --accent, weight increases from 1px to 2px.
focus.$description: Deliberately reuses the exact active-tab visual language (2px accent underline) rather than inventing a new focus treatment.

disabled.$value: Label, value, and border all drop to 40% opacity. No pointer cursor.

error.$value: Bottom border becomes --accent (red). Helper text slot switches to an error message in --accent.
error.$description: Resolves the open question from the full-95 pass: accent-red is now confirmed as a third sanctioned use (active tab/nav state, binary indicators, and error/validation emphasis) — still never used for plain decoration.

success.$value: Not using a dedicated status-green. A checkmark icon in --text-primary is sufficient for form-level success; introducing a new semantic color for this one case isn't worth breaking the monochrome+one-accent discipline.
success.$description: The separate 'should there be a status-green for things like a synced indicator' question is different from form validation and remains open — not resolved by this decision.

species-background-extraction.$description: FINALIZED (3rd and final pass), all 493 Gen 1-4 species. See species-background-colors.json for the lookup table. This methodology went through real course-correction, documented honestly below rather than presenting only the final answer.
history: 1st pass: synthetic hue-average + fixed lightness/saturation target. Abandoned -- fought itself on hue-boundary perception (Gengar's real blue-violet read as plain blue once saturated) and one saturation number didn't fit every species' actual character.

2nd pass: real k-means color clustering (actual sampled pixels, not reconstructed), plus a 'prefer higher saturation' override that turned out to be a real bug -- it let tiny unrepresentative details (an eye pupil, a gem highlight) outrank the genuinely dominant body color, producing wrong picks (Venusaur came back reddish-pink, Wigglytuff came back dark blue-gray).

3rd pass: added explicit contrast-checking against the artwork's own colors, after feedback that automated picks were sometimes too close to blend into the character. This introduced two more real bugs (lightness wandering outside sane light/dark bounds, a stale flagging threshold) before landing correctly -- but the person rejected this entire direction as over-engineered and asked to revert.

FINAL: reverted to the simple 1-151 baseline (original real-cluster extraction, no contrast-solver), with species-by-species manual correction from direct human review -- either a fresh real-color pick, or explicitly reusing another species' exact color pair when two species genuinely look similar (e.g. #121 uses #110's colors, #197 uses #198's, plus 20+ more explicit reuse pairings). For #152-493, the same original simple approach was run, then automatically checked against the curated #1-151 palette for near-matches (RGB distance <35) to reuse rather than mint a new close-but-different color -- 326 of 342 matched. #375 was manually reverted back to its own distinct computed color after the automatic palette-match incorrectly reused a different species' hue for it.
species-background-extraction.final-method-summary: K-means (k=8) on real opaque artwork pixels, excluding near-black/near-white. Predominant color = largest cluster covering >=6% of pixels with saturation >=0.10. No synthetic reconstruction, no automated saturation-boosting, no automated contrast-solver -- those were all tried and rejected. Final say on any individual species always belongs to direct human review, not the algorithm.
species-background-extraction.known-limitation: Cannot fully automate cases where a species' 'identity' color is a small accent rather than the dominant body area (Umbreon's gold rings, Starmie's red gem) -- these needed manual identification.

manual-overrides-applied.$description: Every species individually confirmed or corrected by direct human review, either with its own real color or by explicit reuse of another species' pair.

species-background-extraction.review-status: #1-151: every entry individually confirmed by direct human review (either its own color or an explicit reuse). #152-493: automated real-color extraction, cross-checked against the curated #1-151 palette for reuse, with 23 additional explicit human corrections layered on top. Not every one of the ~493 has been individually eyeballed, but the methodology and known failure modes are well documented, and the highest-visibility species have direct confirmation.

open-items.$description: Explicitly deferred or unresolved — do not treat silence on these as a decision.
items: species_id -> {bg_light, bg_dark} data table — DONE, all 493 species, published to hrezende423/pokeapp-sprites. See species-background-extraction for the full methodology and revision history — the automated contrast-solver direction was tried and explicitly rejected/reverted, not the final approach.
Bento grid and grain-texture techniques — parked for specific future occasions (charts, callout cards), not part of the base system.
Type-badge treatment: both plain colored text (default) and the solid-square badge are sanctioned, dev-time per-context call.
Type color source: both the muted custom palette and the community-standard hex set are sanctioned, dev-time per-context call.
IBM Plex Sans needs to be downloaded and self-hosted as .woff2 — not yet in the codebase.
Status-green for non-form indicators (e.g. a 'synced' status dot) — separate from the form-field success decision (which deliberately avoided a new color), still genuinely open.
Region/generation badge icon (#11) — option C locked with a 'vertical fold line' modification requested but not yet drawn.
7 domain icons (sprite toggle, move category, contest conditions, item categories, berry, type-effectiveness marker, held item) — user sourcing from Tabler/Icones/game-icons.net directly.
Retrofit strategy for pokeapp's existing built modules (old design system) — not yet decided whether/how they migrate to this one.
